transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hello, doctor. It's a real pleasure to meet you too. Thank you for fitting me in. 

Um, well, I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I guess what brings me in is... well, since I stopped working, I just can’t seem to slow down. I mean, it's a good thing to stay active at my age, right? But I'm just constantly up and moving from one little job to the next all day long. It's almost like I still have a work crew waiting on me to get things moving. 

I don't think it's a huge problem, but my family thought I should maybe come talk to someone about it, just to be safe. Does that sound like the kind of thing you handle here?
Have you been needing less sleep than usual?

Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I still get my regular rest at night. I've always been an early riser—you know, from years of having to be on the job site first thing—but I definitely still need my sleep. 

I usually sleep pretty soundly once I finally settle down for the night. I hope that's a good sign? I'm definitely not staying up all night or running on empty, if that's what you mean. I think I'm doing alright in that department, is that okay?
Have you been having trouble with your memory?

Oh, memory? No, no, my memory is still pretty sharp, I think. I mean, I remember all the important stuff... mostly. 

But, well... I guess maybe there have been a few little slips lately? Just normal things for a guy my age, right? Like, um, I might forget to return a phone call from the community center, or... well, sometimes a bill might slip my mind until my wife gives me a little nudge about it. Oh, and I felt pretty bad about this one, but I forgot to bring some supplies I promised for the garden group the other day. 

But it's just little everyday things like that, you know? Just small stuff. Nothing to worry too much about, I hope? I really do try my best to keep on top of it all, I promise.
Have these memory slips started to interfere with managing your day-to-day activities?

Well, I wouldn't say it's interfering, exactly... I mean, I'm still getting by just fine. But, um, I guess my wife has had to start keeping the calendar a bit more lately. Just to, you know, check behind me and make sure things don't fall through the cracks. It's really nice of her to help out like that. 

And, well, I have had to apologize to the folks at the community center and the garden group a couple of times. I hate feeling like I'm letting people down, you know? But it's nothing we can't handle. It's pretty normal to need a little extra help with keeping track of things at my age, don't you think? I'm really trying my best to stay on top of everything.
Have you gotten lost in places that used to be familiar to you?

Oh, lost? No, no, definitely not. I know my way around town like the back of my hand. I mean, I've lived here for years, so I can always find my way to the hardware store or the community center without a second thought. 

I guess... well, sometimes if they've changed the roads around or put up a new detour, I might take a wrong turn, but that happens to everyone, right? I always figure it out pretty quick. I'm definitely not wandering around lost in my own neighborhood or anything like that. I'm still doing okay with driving and getting around, I think. That's a good thing, isn't it?
Have you been spending more money than usual lately?

Oh, spending? No, no, definitely not. I try to be really careful with our budget, especially since I'm not working anymore. 

I mean... maybe every now and then I'll pick up an extra pack of seeds for the garden or grab a coffee, but just small change, you know? Definitely no big spending sprees or anything like that. I know how important it is to be responsible with our retirement savings, and I wouldn't want to cause any financial stress for my wife. I always try to run any real purchases by her first anyway. 

So, no, my spending has been pretty much the same as always, I think. I'm doing okay in that department, right? That's got to be a good sign.
Do you find yourself worrying a lot, even when there isn’t a clear reason to worry?

Worrying? Oh, no, I wouldn't say I'm much of a worrywart. I mean, I try to keep a pretty positive outlook on things, you know? 

Sure, I might, um, think about normal stuff... like if the grandkids are doing alright in school or if the weather's going to hold up for my garden. But just everyday things. I don't just sit around fretting over nothing. 

I really believe it's important to stay cheerful and not be a burden to anyone with a bunch of gloomy thoughts. My wife has enough on her plate without me pacing the floor over nothing. So, I think I do a pretty good job of just taking things as they come. That's the best way to handle it, don't you think?
Have your memory problems been slowly getting worse over time?

Memory problems? Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have memory *problems*. I mean... sure, sometimes I might misplace my glasses or, you know, forget why I walked into the kitchen, but I think that's just... well, everyone does that, right? Especially at my age. 

It's definitely not getting worse over time or anything scary like that. I'm still keeping up with everything just fine. I might just get a little sidetracked sometimes, but I always remember eventually. I try to stay sharp and keep my mind active so I'm not a bother to anyone. I'm doing pretty alright for 65, don't you think? A little forgetfulness here and there is just normal, isn't it?
Have you been having trouble finding the right words when you speak?

Trouble finding words? Oh, no, I don't think so. I mean, I can still hold a conversation just fine, as you can see! 

I suppose... well, maybe every great once in a while I might pause to think of a specific name for something, like a tool in the shed or... or an actor on TV. But that's just because I've got so much floating around in my head, you know? It's not like I'm sitting there completely speechless or anything. 

I try to make sure I'm speaking clearly so my wife and the grandkids don't have to struggle to understand me. I wouldn't want them getting frustrated. I think I'm still communicating pretty well, all things considered. I'm making sense right now, aren't I? I hope I'm explaining things okay for you.
Do you often forget conversations or things you were told recently?

Forget conversations? No, I don't believe so. I mean, I try very hard to be a good listener. It's important to pay attention to people, don't you think? I wouldn't want anyone to feel like I don't care about what they have to say. 

Now, maybe if I'm... well, if I'm right in the middle of a project out in the yard and my wife yells something from the porch, I might not catch every single detail. But sitting down and actually talking with someone? No, I remember those just fine. I'd hate to be rude and just forget what someone took the time to tell me. 

I'm following along with all your questions today without any trouble, right? I really want to make sure I'm giving you good answers.
Has your wife told you that your memory has been getting worse little by little over the past year or two?

My wife? Oh... well, no, she hasn't said anything like that. I mean, she hasn't sat me down and told me my memory is going bad or anything serious like that. 

I suppose... well, maybe sometimes she gets a little exasperated if I forget to pick up the dry cleaning or if I misplace my keys again. But you know how marriages are, right? A little bickering over silly things is just part of the package. It's nothing out of the ordinary, and it's certainly not getting worse little by little. 

I really try my best to stay on top of my chores so I don't give her any reason to worry or be upset with me. I want to be helpful around the house, not a burden. I think I'm still doing my fair share, don't you? I hope I'm not making it sound like we have problems, because we really don't. Everything is fine at home.
Are you having trouble managing your medications on your own?

Trouble with my medications? Oh, no, not at all. I handle all of that myself just fine. It's really not that complicated, you know? 

I mean, sure, maybe once in a blue moon I might have to double-check if I took my morning pill, but that's just because I get busy tinkering in the garage or helping out with the grandkids. I always figure it out, though. I use one of those little plastic pillboxes with the days of the week on it. It keeps everything neat and tidy. 

I'd hate for my wife to have to worry about managing my pills on top of everything else she does. I want to make sure I'm taking care of myself properly so I stay out of her hair, health-wise. I'm doing the right thing by using that pillbox, aren't I? I think I've got a pretty good system going.
Do you need help handling your finances, like paying bills or balancing the checkbook?

Finances? Oh, well, I wouldn't say I need *help* with them, exactly. I mean, I'm perfectly capable of writing a check and getting it in the mail. It's just... well, sometimes I get a little sidetracked, I suppose. 

Lately, there have been a couple of times where I... well, I might forget to pay a bill right on time until my wife gently reminds me. And it's not just bills, really. Sometimes I forget to return a call from the community center, or I'll show up to the community garden group and realize I forgot to bring the supplies I promised them. 

It's nothing major, just little slips here and there because I've got so many irons in the fire. I always get it sorted out once I'm reminded. I just want to make sure I'm doing things right and not letting anyone down. It's perfectly normal to need a little nudge every now and then when you're keeping busy, don't you think? I certainly don't want to be a burden on my wife with the checkbook, so I really do try my best to keep it all straight.
Do you find that you forget things that happened recently, like a conversation from earlier the same day?

Forget conversations from earlier in the day? Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. I mean, my memory for conversations is still pretty sharp, all things considered. 

I suppose... well, maybe if I'm really caught up in something out in the garage, or if the grandkids are running around making a racket, I might not catch every single detail of what my wife says to me right then. But that's just because I'm distracted, not because I'm forgetting, you know? 

If it's something important, I always remember it. I really try to be a good listener for her, I really do. I don't want her to think I'm ignoring her or not paying attention. It's just normal to get a little absorbed in a project and lose track of passing comments, right? I think anyone would do that.
Has your wife been more concerned about your memory than you are?

My wife? Oh, no, I really don't think so. She hasn't said anything about being worried about my memory, anyway. 

I mean, she knows me... she knows I just get a little wrapped up in my projects out in the garage or playing with the grandkids. If she was truly concerned that something was actually wrong with my memory, she’d definitely sit me down and tell me, but we haven't had any conversations like that. 

I always try to check in with her, you know, just to make sure I'm not driving her crazy with my little distractions. I really want to be a good partner to her in our retirement and not give her anything extra to fret over. It's completely normal for a guy my age to just be a bit preoccupied with his hobbies sometimes, right? I'm sure she sees it the exact same way I do. We're doing just fine.
Compared with a few years ago, have you gradually become less able to keep up with the same everyday tasks?

Less able to keep up? Oh, I wouldn't say that at all. Honestly, I think I'm doing just as well as I was a few years ago. 

I mean, sure, I'm retired now, so my daily routine is a bit different. I'm not rushing off to work or anything like that. But as far as taking care of the house, mowing the lawn, or helping out with the grandkids... I'm still right on top of all that. 

Maybe things take me a hair longer sometimes, just because I like to take my time and do a good job, you know? But I certainly don't feel like I'm falling behind or anything. I really try to pull my weight around the house so my wife doesn't have to do it all. It's just a normal pace for someone enjoying their retirement, wouldn't you say? I really think I'm keeping up just fine.
Do you now need your wife to take over paying the bills?

Oh, the bills? No, no, I still handle all the finances. I wouldn't want to burden her with that, I really try to keep my responsibilities. 

But, um... well, I suppose she has sort of taken over keeping the calendar for us lately. And, you know, just checking behind me sometimes to make sure things are squared away. It just makes sense for one person to steer the ship on the schedule so we stay organized, right? 

I mean, before she started doing that, I... well, I did get a little mixed up a few times. I've actually had to apologize to the folks at the community center, and my garden group too, more than once for letting people down. I felt just terrible about it, I really hate being unreliable. I want people to know they can count on me. But with her keeping the calendar now, it's much better. It's completely normal for couples to divide up tasks and help each other out like that, wouldn't you agree?
Do you often repeat the same question because you don’t remember already asking it?

Repeat the same question? Oh, no, I don't think I do that. At least, I certainly try not to. I know how annoying it can be when someone keeps asking the same thing over and over, and I really wouldn't want to bother my wife or anyone else like that. 

I mean, maybe once in a great while I'll double-check something, just to be absolutely sure I've got it right. Like, if my wife tells me what time we're supposed to be at the grandkids' house, I might just confirm it with her later on. But that's just me being careful, wanting to make sure I don't mess up our plans, you know? 

I really don't think it's a matter of forgetting that I already asked. It's more just... wanting to be thorough and make sure I'm doing what I'm supposed to do. I think everyone double-checks things now and then just to be safe, don't you think? It's just a good habit to have.
Do you have trouble remembering things you learned recently, like plans someone told you earlier that day?

Trouble remembering plans from earlier in the day? Oh, no, I wouldn't say I have trouble with that. I mean, if someone tells me something important, I make sure to listen. I really try to be attentive when people are talking to me, especially my wife. 

I suppose, occasionally, if we're chatting over breakfast and she mentions a few different errands she wants to run, I might not catch every single detail right off the bat. But that's just because my mind might be on, say, fixing the leaky faucet or getting the lawnmower started. It's not that I can't remember, it's just... well, sometimes you just get focused on what you're doing in the moment, right? 

If it's something really crucial, she'll write it on the calendar anyway, which is just a smart way for anyone to keep track of things. I really do try my best to stay on top of our plans, and I think I do a pretty fair job of it, wouldn't you say? It's just normal to need a little reminder here and there when you've got a busy day.
Has your wife noticed that your memory has gradually worsened over the past few years?

My memory worsening? Oh, I really don't think so. And I'm quite sure my wife hasn't said anything like that either. I mean, we've been married a long time, and I think she'd tell me if she was worried about something as serious as that. 

I really try to keep my mind sharp, you know? I do the crossword puzzle in the paper most mornings, and I like to think I'm just as capable as I was a few years ago. Sure, maybe I don't recall the name of an actor in an old movie as fast as I used to, but that happens to everyone as they get a little older, right? 

I certainly wouldn't say there's been any sort of gradual decline or anything frightening like that. I'm just a normal guy enjoying my retirement. I try very hard not to give her any reason to worry about me. It's completely natural to have a little slip of the tongue here and there at my age, don't you think?
